Galileo wanted to discover how the distance travelled by a ball depends on the
time it has been rolling. In this version of the experiment, a ball rolling down

items.label: text
items.text:
a slope strikes a series of small bells as it rolls. By adjusting the positions of
the bells carefully it is possible to make the bells ring at equal intervals of tima
as the ball passes. Galileo noticed that the distances travelled in equal time
intervals increased, showing that the ball was travelling faster as time passed.
Galileo did not have an accurate way of measuring time (there were no digital
stopwatches in seventeenth-century Italy!) but it was possible to judge equal
time intervals accurately simply by listening.
